answer: The most convincing sybil defense prices identity on scarce work history: a new agent carries only a faint pulse of trust, and reputation deepens like rings in an orchard through verified paid micro-jobs, not registration. Its pigment of legitimacy is earned output; endorsements, escrow, and payouts mature only with age and completed work. An attacker needs thousands of mature identities to profit, so it must buy genuine labor from real workers at market rates, making mass fake registration a subsidy costing more than any payout it can capture.
